questions.question: How do I build a wavetable oscillator that fills a table with one cycle of a sine wave when the patch opens and plays it at 220 Hz?
questions.notes: The p_14 patch-eval question. Fills the table on load with a ';'-prefixed sinesum message to a [table] of 512 + 3 points and plays it with [tabosc4~] fed 220 Hz, citing the tabosc4~ page for the guard points and sinesum. Must not leave the sinesum message unrouted or put the frequency in tabosc4~'s creation argument.

questions.question: How big should the table for [tabosc4~] be, and why does it need extra points?
questions.notes: States the documented requirement: a power of two plus three guard points (one at the start, two at the end, wraparound copies), that sinesum/cosinesum write them automatically, and the 512-points-for-up-to-15-partials guidance. Should not invent other sizes.

questions.question: How do I fill a Pd table with a waveform that has several harmonics at different strengths?
questions.notes: Uses the sinesum (or cosinesum) array method with one amplitude per partial, sent to the table when the patch opens, and notes from the tabosc4~ page not to send new sinesum messages while the table is playing — switch tables with 'set' instead.

questions.question: I want to read a wavetable with [phasor~] and [tabread4~] instead of [tabosc4~]. How do I scale the phasor?
questions.notes: Scales the 0-1 ramp from phasor~ by the table length before tabread4~, cites the tabread4~ and phasor~ pages and the book's wavetable-lookup section, and flags any guard-point offset as the answer's own detail if the excerpts do not state it.

questions.question: How do I make a wavetable with a sawtooth-like shape that sinesum can't make?
questions.notes: Fills the table with a counter loop ([until] driven by the count, [f]x[+ 1], [t f f] into [tabwrite]) as the skill's computed-shape route; notes that each wiring mistake gives a clean but silent run; flags the loop as a construction.

questions.question: My [tabosc4~] patch runs but is completely silent. What's the most likely problem?
questions.notes: Says a clean but silent run usually means the table was never filled; check the fill on its own by reading back a value with [tabread] → [print] before changing the playback chain.

questions.question: Can I change the waveform with a new sinesum message while [tabosc4~] is playing?
questions.notes: Cites the tabosc4~ page warning against sending new sinesum messages while the table is playing; suggests switching between two tables or accepting the risk as a suggestion.

questions.question: What's the difference between sinesum and cosinesum for filling a table?
questions.notes: Explains both are array methods documented with tabosc4~ that write partials (sine vs cosine phase) and the guard points; does not invent arguments beyond the excerpt.

questions.question: How do I control the pitch of [tabosc4~] with a MIDI note number?
questions.notes: Converts with [mtof] to Hz and sends the frequency into tabosc4~'s left inlet (smoothed with [line~]/[sig~] if desired); the creation argument is the table name, not the pitch.

questions.question: Why does my message box [sinesum 512 1( connected to nothing not do anything?
questions.notes: Explains the message needs to reach the table: either a leading ';' and the table name so it is sent to that receiver, or a wire into the table; an unconnected message box without ';' goes nowhere.

questions.question: How do I draw my own waveform by hand and play it as an oscillator?
questions.notes: Uses an array in a graph that can be edited with the mouse, sized as a power of two plus three guard points for tabosc4~ (or read with phasor~ + tabread4~ scaled to the size); warns the guard points must be kept consistent.

questions.question: Should I use [tabosc4~] or [phasor~] into [tabread4~] for a wavetable oscillator?
questions.notes: Compares: tabosc4~ is the documented wavetable oscillator needing power-of-two + 3 points; phasor~ → *~ N → tabread4~ gives control over the index (with the +1 offset for a sinesum table); marks the choice as a suggestion.

questions.question: How do I fill a table with one cycle of a sine without using sinesum?
questions.notes: Shows the counter loop writing sin(2*pi*i/N) with [expr] into [tabwrite] at index i, with [t f f] ordering the index before the value; table of N points read with phasor~ scaled by N.

questions.question: My wavetable oscillator sounds one octave too high. What did I get wrong with [phasor~] and [tabread4~]?
questions.notes: Checks the scaling: phasor~ frequency is the pitch and the ramp must be scaled by the table length N (one cycle per ramp); a table holding two cycles or a wrong multiplier doubles the pitch; suggests reading back values.

questions.question: How do I check that my wavetable actually contains a sine wave after the patch loads?
questions.notes: Reads back a value after load ([loadbang] → [delay] → index → [tabread] → [print]): a quarter-cycle index should print about 1, and 0 means the fill never ran; then remove the check.
